action: Introduce a drought-compatible legume cover crop/intercrop
why: Legumes can add biologically fixed nitrogen while maintaining soil cover, helping support soil function under water-limited conditions.
time_horizon: Short term: one growing season for establishment

expected_impact.target: Track improvement from the baseline over successive growing seasons
expected_impact.measurement: Measure soil organic carbon periodically using soil testing

monitoring: Record baseline soil organic carbon, soil moisture and plant diversity before implementation, then compare measurements after each growing season.
evidence_summary: FAO resources describe the role of biodiversity-friendly agricultural practices, including crop diversification and cover crops, in supporting soil and ecosystem functions.

why: A structurally different vegetation strip can provide additional habitat and resources for organisms, increasing habitat diversity and supporting species richness.
time_horizon: Short term: establishment; medium term: 2-5 years for habitat development

expected_impact.target: Increase the diversity of habitat features and observed species relative to the baseline
expected_impact.measurement: Record habitat types and conduct periodic plant, insect and other species observations

monitoring: Record the baseline number and types of habitat features and observed species, then repeat biodiversity observations periodically.
evidence_summary: FAO and biodiversity indicator resources describe habitat diversity and vegetation structure as important components of agricultural biodiversity.

why: Agroforestry can add vertical and seasonal vegetation structure, providing additional habitat while improving landscape diversity and potentially supporting soil and water functions.
time_horizon: Medium term: 2-5 years for establishment; longer-term benefits as vegetation matures

expected_impact.target: Increase structural and plant diversity relative to the baseline
expected_impact.measurement: Monitor tree and shrub establishment, vegetation diversity and periodic species observations

monitoring: Record the number and type of established trees and shrubs and repeat vegetation and biodiversity observations over time.
evidence_summary: FAO agroforestry resources describe how trees integrated into agricultural landscapes can provide habitat, improve vegetation structure and contribute to multiple ecosystem functions.

why: Maintaining soil cover and adding appropriate organic inputs can protect soil from erosion, support soil biological activity and contribute to maintaining or increasing soil organic carbon.
time_horizon: Short term: one growing season for cover establishment; medium term: multiple seasons for measurable soil-carbon change

expected_impact.metric: soil organic carbon and soil cover
expected_impact.target: Maintain or increase soil organic carbon relative to the baseline while increasing soil surface cover
expected_impact.measurement: Conduct periodic soil organic carbon testing and estimate the percentage of soil covered

monitoring: Measure baseline soil organic carbon and soil-cover percentage, then compare results after each growing season.
evidence_summary: FAO soil resources and USDA NRCS guidance describe soil cover and organic inputs as important practices for maintaining soil health and supporting soil organic matter.

action: Create or restore habitat connections between fragmented areas
why: Connecting suitable habitat patches can improve landscape connectivity, allowing species to move between habitat areas and potentially reducing the effects of habitat fragmentation.
time_horizon: Medium to long term: 2-10+ years depending on habitat restoration and vegetation establishment

expected_impact.target: Increase connected habitat area and reduce gaps between suitable habitat patches relative to the baseline
expected_impact.measurement: Map habitat patches and monitor connectivity together with periodic biodiversity observations

monitoring: Map baseline habitat patches and connections, then compare habitat connectivity and observed biodiversity at regular monitoring intervals.
evidence_summary: IUCN resources describe ecological connectivity as important for maintaining ecological processes and enabling species movement between habitat areas.
